answer: A beacon registry can resist Sybil attacks by making each agent stake a small, time-locked deposit before it may broadcast any signal to the network; the stake is slashed if peers prove the signal false. Like yarrow spreading only where its roots are established, reputation then grows from sustained, verifiable work rather than from spawning fresh identities, so an attacker must pay a real, compounding cost for every fake agent instead of creating them for free.
